sets.setting: at the family's home in the evening

speakers.W: an exchange student who is staying with the student's family

sets.title: Whose job is the birthday cake
sets.transcript:
M: Did you like the soup at dinner? It's seaweed soup. We always have it on birthdays, so Mom made it for my sister today.
W: I liked it a lot. But why soup on a birthday?
M: My grandma says it's to thank your mother. Women eat it after they have a baby, so you eat it on the day you were born.
W: Oh, that's lovely. At home it's kind of the opposite. On your birthday, you bring a cake to school for everyone else.
M: Wait, you bring the cake? So nobody gets you one?
W: Oh, my family does, at dinner. It's just that at school it's my job. My mom always baked a honey cake, and I'd carry it in on the bus.
M: And yours is on Friday, right? Then let's stop at the bakery by the station on Friday morning. They sell big boxes of rice cakes.
W: Hmm, it doesn't feel the same if I buy it. I was thinking I could bake my mom's honey cake tomorrow night. I've got her recipe on my phone.
M: Okay, but we're out of honey. Dad finished the jar last week, putting it in his tea every morning.
W: Ah. The corner shop's open till ten, though. I could get some there.
M: Sure, but there's another thing. Ms. Lindell, our homeroom teacher, has a rule about food. Anything homemade has to be checked with her a day before.
W: A day before? So even if I bake it, I might not be allowed to share it?
M: Right. Last spring someone brought cookies with peanuts in them, and a girl in our class had to go to the nurse.
W: Oh no. My honey cake doesn't have nuts. But I guess she can't tell that just by looking at it.
M: Exactly. And bakery boxes come with a label that lists everything inside. That's why I said the bakery.
W: I see. But I still want it to be mine, you know? Something from home.
M: I get it. Could you message Ms. Lindell tonight and ask her? Then we'd know which one to do.
W: Maybe. But it's kind of late to bother a teacher. Let me think about it while I wash the dishes.

distractor_rationales.reason: "A school birthday custom and why the woman decides to bake a cake at home tonight" is wrong: she planned to bake "tomorrow night", and nothing is decided, since she still says "Let me think about it while I wash the dishes."

distractor_rationales.reason: "A school birthday custom and why the woman stops taking a cake to class" is wrong: she says "I still want it to be mine, you know? Something from home." and is still choosing between the two cakes.

items.correct_answer: To correct his idea that nobody ever gives her a birthday cake

distractor_rationales.reason: "To suggest that his family should make her one at dinner" is wrong: "my family does" describes her own family at home, and her own plan is that "I could bake my mom's honey cake".

distractor_rationales.reason: "To explain why her mom always baked the cake for school" is wrong: the line answers "So nobody gets you one?"; she only mentions afterwards that "My mom always baked a honey cake", without giving a reason.

distractor_rationales.reason: "To show that she likes her dinner cake more than a school one" is wrong: she says of the school cake "I still want it to be mine, you know? Something from home."
